definition: Effective accelerationism (e/acc) is a 21st-century ideological movement that advocates for an explicitly pro-technology stance.
details: Its proponents believe that unrestricted technological progress, especially driven by artificial intelligence, is a solution to universal human problems, such as poverty, war, and climate change. They perceive themselves as a counterweight to more cautious views on technological innovation and often label their opponents derogatorily as "doomers" or "decels" (short for decelerationists). The movement carries utopian undertones and advocates for faster AI progress to ensure human survival and propagate consciousness throughout the universe. Although effective accelerationism has been described as a fringe movement and as cult-like, it has gained mainstream visibility in 2023. A number of high-profile Silicon Valley figures, including investors Marc Andreessen and Garry Tan, explicitly endorsed it by adding "e/acc" to their public social media profiles.

explainer.lead: Effective accelerationism, or e/acc, argues that society should push technology—especially artificial intelligence—forward with fewer restrictions. Its appeal lies in a sweeping promise: faster progress could help solve humanity’s biggest problems, while its clash with more cautious approaches makes it an important position in debates over AI’s future.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a group of people building a very powerful new kind of engine. Some want to slow down and check the risks, but e/acc supporters want to speed up because they believe the engine could help end poverty, stop wars, and fight climate change. They see caution as an obstacle to a better future.
tiers.practitioner: For an engineer, e/acc is not an algorithm, architecture, or deployment method, but a stance that favors faster AI development with fewer restrictions. It may shape arguments around product and research priorities rather than prescribe tools or settings. A key pitfall is treating speed itself as evidence of benefit, or dismissing legitimate caution by labeling critics “doomers” or “decels.”
tiers.paperLevel: Effective accelerationism is a 21st-century ideological movement defined by an explicitly pro-technology position: unrestricted technological progress, particularly progress driven by AI, is treated as a solution to universal human problems such as poverty, war, and climate change. Its utopian program links faster AI progress to human survival and the propagation of consciousness throughout the universe; it is a normative position rather than a formal model with an equation. It has been described as fringe and cult-like, although it gained mainstream visibility in 2023.

explainer.example: Marc Andreessen and Garry Tan publicly endorsed the movement by adding “e/acc” to their social-media profiles. This was a concrete declaration of support for acceleration, not evidence by itself that unrestricted AI progress would solve the problems the movement names.

explainer.intuition: The core intuition is that technological progress creates capabilities humanity needs, so delaying it also delays solutions. E/acc extends this idea into a utopian claim that accelerating AI can help secure human survival and spread consciousness beyond Earth.
howItWorks: Adopt an explicitly pro-technology stance rather than treating restraint as the default.
Regard unrestricted progress, especially AI-driven progress, as a route to solving poverty, war, and climate change.
Push for faster AI progress as a counterweight to cautious views on innovation.
Link acceleration to the larger goals of human survival and propagating consciousness throughout the universe.
Signal allegiance with labels such as “e/acc,” while sometimes calling opponents “doomers” or “decels.”
explainer.whyItMatters: E/acc gives a clear voice to the case for speeding up AI rather than slowing it down, framing caution itself as a threat to human progress and survival. Its mainstream visibility in 2023 brought this once-fringe position into wider public view.
misconceptions: E/acc is not a technical AI method: it offers no model, training procedure, or engineering recipe.
Supporting faster AI does not, by itself, demonstrate that unrestricted progress will solve poverty, war, or climate change.
Its dismissive labels for critics do not mean every cautious position rejects technology altogether.
